question: Did Saul's family die with him?
summary: 1 Chronicles 10:6 says "Saul died, and his three sons, and all his house died together." 2 Samuel 2:1-7 then has Ishbosheth — Saul's son — made king of Israel after Saul's death. 2 Samuel 21 has David later handing over seven of Saul's descendants to be hanged. The "all his house died together" claim is contradicted by surviving family members appearing throughout 2 Samuel.

reconcile.connective: Defenders limit "all his house" to the kin and courtiers present at Gilboa, noting Chronicles itself names survivors elsewhere.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells presses the plain wording: Chronicles says Saul's whole house died together, yet Samuel keeps producing living sons and grandsons of Saul.

pd_work.note: Treats this passage directly: reads 'all his house' as those present at the battle and notes Ish-bosheth and Mephibosheth were kept at Gibeah and survived. Row-surfaced harmonizer used because Haley's coverage of this specific subtotal could not be confirmed.

link.title: 1 Chronicles 10:6 — Did all of Saul's family die with him or not?
link.note: Live, on-topic apologetic page; harmonizes 'all his house' as those who followed Saul to war, citing Ishbosheth's and Mephibosheth's survival.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Saul died, and his three sons, and all his house—his sons and courtiers who were there engaged in the battle. But it appears that Ish-bosheth and Mephibosheth were kept at Gibeah on account of their youth.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly restricts the scope of 'all his house' to those present at Gilboa and names the surviving sons (Ish-bosheth, Mephibosheth) who reappear in 2 Samuel — the exact harmonization for this row.
